messages.subject: Add covariates from multiple rasters
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to bring in multiple rasters to add covariates to my mask, but I am having issues with my second raster (which is a DEM elevation model). My first raster is classified habitat data with codes for various habitat types, and I have no trouble running a model with this data (which I did not include here due to the very large file size of the rasters):

###Load and Prepare SECR capture history
lsCH <- read.capthist('lscapt.txt', 'lstrap.txt', detector = 'count', covnames = c("sex"))

#2km habitat mask
lsmask_2km <- make.mask(traps, buffer = 15000, spacing = 2000, type = "trapbuffer")
#Loading Raster
ls_hab <- raster("LittleSmoky_Hab_30m.tif", verbose=FALSE)
#turn to polygon, secr doens't like raster
hab_poly <- as(ls_hab, "SpatialGridDataFrame")
##rename columns
names(hab_poly) <- "hab"
###Add hab values to mask
LS_2km_mask <- addCovariates(lsmask_2km, hab_poly)

##Model NULL
ls.fit.NULL.2km <- secr.fit(lsCH,mask=LS_2km_mask, trace=FALSE, method = 'Nelder-Mead') 
##Model D~habitat
ls.fit.D.hab.2km <- secr.fit(lsCH,mask=LS_2km_mask,model=list(D~hab), trace=FALSE, method = 'Nelder-Mead') 


I get no errors when running these. When I add in the elevation raster, I don't get errors when it is brought in and joined to the mask:

#Loading Raster
ls_elev <- raster("LittleSmoky_Elevation.tif", verbose=FALSE)
#turn to polygon, secr doens't like raster
elev_poly <- as(ls_elev, "SpatialGridDataFrame")
##rename columns
names(elev_poly) <- "elev"
###Add hab values to mask
LS_2km_mask <- addCovariates(LS_2km_mask, elev_poly)

However, when I try to run the same model as above but with D~elev, I get the following errors:
##Model D~elev
ls.fit.D.elev.2km <- secr.fit(lsCH,mask=LS_2km_mask,model=list(D~elev), trace=FALSE, method = 'Nelder-Mead')

densities : Inf Inf Inf Inf Inf Inf
densities : Inf Inf Inf Inf Inf Inf
densities : Inf Inf Inf Inf Inf Inf
densities : Inf Inf Inf Inf Inf Inf
densities : Inf Inf Inf Inf Inf Inf
There were 50 or more warnings (use warnings() to see the first 50)

I transformed the elevation data to be the same resolution as my habitat data (30x30m):

resolution  : 30, 30  (x, y)
extent      : -1203613, -888882.9, -130863.2, 151466.8  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
coord. ref. : +proj=tmerc +lat_0=55 +lon_0=-102 +k=1 +x_0=0 +y_0=0 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs +ellps=WGS84 +towgs84=0,0,0
data source : C:\Users\sammc\Documents\Google Drive\PhD\R\Caribou Script\Little Smoky\LittleSmoky_Elevation.tif
names       : LittleSmoky_Elevation
values      : 527, 3955  (min, max)

I am having trouble getting the extent to match exactly. Is this where my problem lies? Talking with a coworker who is not an R user but has experience with rasters thinks they need to be the exact same extent. I saw in the forum an offline response from Borchers for extracting raster data, but this also does not work for me:

covariates(LS_2km_mask) <- data.frame(Habitat = extract(ls_elev, LS_2km_mask, spatial = TRUE) # extract at mask coordinates and put them in the mask covariate named "Habitat"

Do elevation models need to be brought in differently than other covariate surfaces such as habitat? I also want to use slope and aspect rasters (that are produced from my elevation raster) in the future as well.

Any help would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you,
Sam

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Add covariates from multiple rasters
parts:
Hi
I cannot see what is going on here.It's not necessary to match extents or resolution, except that obviously the data source should cover all mask cells, nor do I know of anything special about elevation models. Of the three masks in the RData file you attached, only one has a covariate and that is not 'elev'. I suggest focussing on getting the mask right before fitting any model. I know that's what you're trying to do, but dig deeper with checks like
head(covariates(LS_2km_mask))
table(covariates(LS_2km_mask)$hab)
plot(LS_2km_mask, covariate = 'hab', xy='bottomright')

(My impression is that your habitat types are highly interspersed: every feasible home range will include nearly the same mix of types, so type is unlikely to be predictive of density.  Using numeric codes for habitat classes is dangerous: convert to factor. And I am almost certain you cannot have enough data or patience to fit 10 levels, most of which relate to very small areas.)
Murray
